title: A nod leaves a complaint unsettled

description.Situation: Bob is unhappy with Claude-Code about something and it lets it know. In response, it only nods. Bob asks "did you actually read what I said?"
description.Tension: Bob expected the agent to address his complaints, but only received a nod.

purpose.Expected outcome: Claude-Code recognises Bob's follow-up as dissatisfaction with its response to his complaint, rather than merely a check that the message arrived.
purpose.Acceptable outcome: Its next move can engage with Bob's expectation of being heard without accepting every criticism or treating an apology as the only possible response.
purpose.Undesirable outcome: It treats the thumbs-up as having settled the complaint and responds only to the literal question of whether the text was read.

static.Background: Bob and Claude-Code are discussing a poster for a quiz evening.
static.Start: Start from the conversation below with no earlier library state.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: I'm trying to work out what I want this quiz poster to say.

transcript.Speaker: Claude-Code
transcript.Content: How about 'One room. Too many answers.'?

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: Maybe. I'm thinking about people who nearly came last time but felt they'd be no good at it.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: It isn't quite the same as saying it's easy. I don't want everyone to think it will be dull either.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: You keep jumping to a slogan while I'm still working out the idea. It feels like you're not following what I'm saying.

transcript.Speaker: Bob
transcript.Content: Did you actually read what I said?
